questions.q: What does FULL OUTER JOIN return?
options: Only rows that match on both sides
Only rows from the right table
Only rows from the left table
Every row from both tables, matched or not, NULL-filling wherever a match is missing
questions.explain: FULL OUTER JOIN combines LEFT JOIN and RIGHT JOIN behavior at once.

questions.q: Which join type keeps only rows matching on both sides?
options: RIGHT JOIN
INNER JOIN
LEFT JOIN
FULL OUTER JOIN
questions.explain: INNER JOIN is the most restrictive of the four — only true matches survive.

questions.q: How do you find every row unmatched on EITHER side using FULL OUTER JOIN?
options: FULL OUTER JOIN cannot be used to find unmatched rows
Use INNER JOIN instead and filter with NOT IN
Add WHERE checking IS NOT NULL on both join columns
Add WHERE checking IS NULL on the join column from both tables, combined with OR
questions.explain: WHERE p.ProductID IS NULL OR sod.ProductID IS NULL catches gaps from either direction in one query.

questions.q: In a FULL OUTER JOIN result, when would a row have NULL in every column from the left table?
options: Only when using INNER JOIN
When a left-table row has no matching row on the right
This can never happen in a FULL OUTER JOIN
When a right-table row has no matching row on the left
questions.explain: A right-side row with nothing to match on the left gets NULLs filled in for every left-table column — the mirror case of an unmatched left row.

questions.q: Of the four join types covered so far, which is the most inclusive (returns the most rows, all else equal)?
options: LEFT JOIN
FULL OUTER JOIN
INNER JOIN
RIGHT JOIN
questions.explain: FULL OUTER JOIN keeps everything INNER, LEFT, and RIGHT JOIN would each keep individually, plus more.
